title: Cummal cooidjagh
description: Ten short stories about society and living together: a widow's donation to a village library, a shared garden on a hillside, a town cleaning its emptied dock, a refugee girl telling her family's story, the judges' panel at a village baking competition, a village meeting split into two factions, Hallowe'en beliefs told by a grandmother, a community pantomime about a sultan, an astronomy club in a village hall, and a parish pilgrimage walk.

lessons.title: Toyrtys da'n lioarlann
lessons.summary: Clemency Wardle is the librarian of the small library in Laxey; the widow Hortense Beckwith offers it a donation: the four hundred books of her late husband Lancelot, a famous writer of horror stories, and a portrait of him; some people in the village grumble that horror books are bad for children, and Clemency answers in a letter to the paper that the library is for everyone and that the horror books stand on their own shelf for adults; she and Hortense gather the books from the big house, and the evening when the portrait is hung is pleasant, even for the man who grumbled.
lessons.text:
Ta Clemency Wardle ny lioarlannee ayns Laksaa. Ta'n lioarlann beg, agh t'ee lane dy chooilley laa. Ta paitçhyn çheet stiagh lurg y scoill, as ta shenn sleih lhaih ny pabyryn-naight. Ta'n lioarlannee credjal dy vel lioarlann myr cree y valley, er-y-fa dy vel sleih dy chooilley sorçh çheet cooidjagh ayn.

Moghrey Jemayrt, haink ben stiagh as eddin trimshagh eck. Hortense Beckwith v'ee, treoghe Lancelot Beckwith. V'eh ny screeudeyr ennymoil, as hooar eh baase y vlein shen chaie. Va lioaryn grinderys echey: skeealyn mychione thieyn dorraghey 'sy oie, as sleih marroo çheet erash.

“S'treoghe mee nish,” dooyrt Hortense, “as ta'n thie ro vooar dou. Ta kiare cheead lioar ayn. Bare lhiam toyrtys y chur da'n lioarlann: ny lioaryn echey ooilley, as cochaslys Lancelot neesht. Ren peinteyr ennymoil y cochaslys shen.”

Va Clemency feer booiagh. Cha row toyrtys cho mooar shen rieau er ve currit da'n lioarlann.

Agh tra va'n naight er goll mygeayrt y valley, va accan ec kuse dy leih. “Cha nel grinderys mie son paitçhyn,” dooyrt fer. “Ta ny skeealyn shen ro ghorraghey.” Eisht ren ee lettyr y screeu da'n phabyr-naight:

“Ta lioarlann son dy chooilley pheiagh. Bee ny lioaryn grinderys er nyn shelg hene, son sleih aasit. Dy mynchooishagh, ta mee laccal gra dy row Lancelot Beckwith ny ghooinney mie. V'eh screeu skeealyn dorraghey, agh v'eh cur argid da'n scoill dy chooilley vlein. Cha nel shin laccal accan, agh shin laccal lhaihderyn.”

Er y Jesarn, hie Clemency as Hortense dys y thie mooar. Va lioaryn ayns dagh shamyr: er y laare, fo'n stoyl, as eer 'sy chuishlin. Ren ad ny lioaryn y hymsaghey ayns kishtaghyn, as v'ad çhymsaghey rish shiaght ooryn. “Shoh lioar mynchooishagh,” dooyrt Hortense, as lioar veg ghorrym ayns e laue. “Ren eh y chied skeeal echey y screeu ayns y lioar shoh.”

Shiaghtin ny lurg shen, va fastyr taitnyssagh 'sy lioarlann. Va cochaslys Lancelot er y voalley, as va tey as arran millish ayn son dy chooilley pheiagh. Ren Hortense loayrt mychione y dooinney eck, as ren ny paitçhyn gearey. Haink eer y fer va accan echey. “Va shoh taitnyssagh,” dooyrt eh rish y lioarlannee, “as ta mee er ghoaill lioar grinderys hym hene.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Clemency Wardle?
She lioarlannee ee ayns y lioarlann veg ayns Laksaa.
Quoi v'ayn Lancelot Beckwith?
V'eh ny screeudeyr ennymoil, as v'eh screeu lioaryn grinderys.
Cre va'n toyrtys hug Hortense da'n lioarlann?
Hug ee kiare cheead lioar da'n lioarlann, as cochaslys Lancelot neesht.
Quoi ta Hortense Beckwith?
She treoghe Lancelot Beckwith ee.
Cre'n accan va ec kuse dy leih?
Dooyrt ad nagh vel grinderys mie son paitçhyn.
Cre ren Clemency as Hortense er y Jesarn?
Ren ad ny lioaryn y hymsaghey ayns kishtaghyn ayns y thie mooar.
Cre va mynchooishagh mychione y lioar veg ghorrym?
Ren Lancelot y chied skeeal echey y screeu ayns y lioar shen.
Row'n fastyr 'sy lioarlann taitnyssagh?
Va. Va'n fastyr feer taitnyssagh, eer son y fer va accan echey.

lessons.title: Y garey er y lhargagh
lessons.summary: Behind the houses in Andreas there is a shared garden on a hillside, and the retired postman Rowland Pettigrew looks after it with his ten-year-old neighbour Caspar: at the bottom of the slope the ground is damp and they grow watercress in the clean water of the stream, and ferns grow under an old ash tree; a rodent starts eating the seeds, and a neighbour wants poison, but Rowland says no: an owl lives in the ash tree and hunts at night, and a cat with white paws watches by day; finches sing in the bushes, and in the end the neighbours share the watercress.
lessons.text:
Cooyl ny thieyn ayns Andreas, ta garey er lhargagh ard. She garey cooidjagh eh: ta dagh lught-thie ec y traid gobbraghey ayn, as ta ny praaseyn as ny blaaghyn son dy chooilley pheiagh. Ta Rowland Pettigrew, va ny phostagh rish daeed blein, kiarail jeh'n gharey nish. Dy mennick, ta Caspar, y guilley jeh jeih bleeaney ta cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee gobbraghey marish.

Ta'n lhargagh feer ard. Ec baare y lhargagh, ta'n thalloo mie, agh ec y bun, faggys da'n strooan, ta tashey 'sy thalloo dy kinjagh. “Cha nel ny praaseyn gaase dy mie ayns y tashey shen,” dooyrt Rowland rish Caspar. “Agh ta lus ayn ta laccal tashey as ushtey glen: burley.” Myr shen, ren ad burley y chur ayns ushtey y strooan. Ta'n burley glass as geyre, as s'mie lesh ny naboonyn eh ayns arran.

Ec mean y lhargagh, ta unjin shenn. Ta'n unjin shoh ny smoo na keead blein dy eash. Fo ny banglaneyn echey, ta rhennee gaase, glass as aalin. Cha nel Rowland giarey ny rhennee, er-y-fa dy vel ad freayll y thalloo fliugh fo'n unjin.

Ayns Averil, va boirey ayn. Va caigneyder ennagh gee ny rassyn. Dagh moghrey, va tuill veggey 'sy thalloo, as va ny rassyn ersooyl. “Lugh t'ayn, ny roddan,” dooyrt Caspar. Haink naboo, as ec y traa cheddin dooyrt eh: “Cur nieu er y thalloo! Ver shen jerrey er ny caigneyderyn.”

“Cha der,” dooyrt Rowland. “Ta paitçhyn as moddee cloie 'sy gharey. As ta carrey ain hene ayn.” Ghow eh Caspar dys yn unjin 'sy fastyr. Ayns tuill mooar 'sy villey, va hullad ny soie. “T'ee goll magh 'syn oie,” dooyrt Rowland, “as t'ee gee lughee as roddanyn. Cha nel caigneyder erbee sauçhey tra ta'n hullad shelg.”

Ec y traa cheddin, va kayt ec Caspar, kayt doo as spaag vane echey er dagh cass. Va'n kayt soie ec y strooan 'sy laa, as eh freayll arrey er y thalloo. Va daa spaag echey er y chreg, as y daa spaag elley aarloo dy lheim.

Lurg shiaghtin, va ny rassyn sauçhey. Va'n hullad shelg 'syn oie, as va'n kayt shelg 'sy laa. Va ny corkanyn goaill arraneyn ayns y tom, as cha row aggle orroo. Ta ny corkanyn gee rassyn neesht, agh cha nel ad gee monney.

Ayns Mean Souree, va ny naboonyn ooilley giarey yn burley. Hooar dagh lught-thie ayrn jeh'n burley.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta kiarail jeh'n gharey cooidjagh?
Ta Rowland Pettigrew kiarail jeh, as ta Caspar gobbraghey marish.
C'raad ta burley gaase?
Ta burley gaase ayns ushtey y strooan ec bun y lhargagh, raad ta tashey 'sy thalloo.
Cre ta gaase fo'n unjin?
Ta rhennee gaase fo'n unjin.
Cre'n fa nagh ren Rowland nieu y chur er y thalloo?
Er-y-fa dy vel paitçhyn as moddee cloie 'sy gharey, as dy vel hullad shelg ny caigneyderyn.
Cre ta ny corkanyn jannoo?
Ta ny corkanyn goaill arraneyn ayns y tom.

lessons.title: Laa ayns y calloo follym
lessons.summary: In Ramsey the old dock of the harbour is emptied so that its walls can be mended, and the town is asked to help clean it; the retired sailor Obadiah Penketh, seventy-eight, brings his granddaughter Wenna and his old hand cart: at the bottom of the empty dock lies a thick layer of sediment, and in it they find seaweed, an old lobster pot with a lobster still in it, and a penny from 1911; Obadiah tells Wenna about his years at sea, puts the lobster back into the sea, ties the seaweed on the cart with a leather strap and takes it to the shared gardens, and Wenna keeps the penny.
lessons.text:
Ayns Rhumsaa, ta calloo shenn ec y phurt. Ta ny boallaghyn echey er ve brisht, as she egin daue ve jeant noa. Myr shen, va'n calloo goll er folmaghey ayns y Vee Boaldyn. Hie yn ushtey magh trooid y yiat, oor lurg oor, derrey nagh row agh laagh ec y bun. Va lettyr ayns y phabyr-naight: “Ta'n folmaghey jeant. Tar as cur laue dooin y calloo y ghlenney er y Jesarn!”

Ta Obadiah Penketh hoght bleeaney as tree-feed. V'eh ny varrinagh rish daeed blein, as ren eh shiaull dys America, dys yn Affrick as dys y Çhapaan. Nish t'eh cummal ayns thie beg ec y phurt. Er y Jesarn, ghow eh e inneen-vac Wenna lesh, as e chairt shenn neesht: cairt veg fuyghagh, as daa wheeyl er.

“Va mee ny marrinagh aeg ayns y calloo shoh,” dooyrt Obadiah. “Cha vaik mee rieau eh follym.”

Va drundin ooilley er y laare: drundin doo as trome, as va ny sleih ayn derrey ny glioonyn. Va ny marrinee as ny eeasteyryn shenn er jeet, as ny paitçhyn neesht, as v'ad ooilley gobbraghey cooidjagh. Ayns y drundin, va famlagh dy liooar, famlagh doo as famlagh dhone. Va coyrd shenn as kishtaghyn gimmee ayn neesht.

Hooar Wenna kishtey gimmee shenn 'sy drundin. Va gimmagh beg ayn foast, bio! “She egin dooin eh y chur erash 'sy cheayn,” dooyrt Obadiah. Ren eh y gimmagh y ghoaill dys y traie, as hie y gimmagh ersooyl fo'n ushtey.

Eisht hooar Wenna red beg cruinn. Ping v'ayn, ping shenn veih'n vlein 1911. “Va'n ping shoh 'sy drundin rish keead blein,” dooyrt Obadiah. “Tra va mee my ghuilley, va shin kionnaghey arran millish son daa phing.”

Va'n famlagh ry-gheddyn er dy chooilley laue. Ren Obadiah y famlagh y hymsaghey er y chairt. Eisht ren eh y famlagh y chiangley er y chairt lesh yeeal: yeeal liauyr jeh crackan, va echey er y lhong rish ymmodee bleeantyn. “Ta'n yeeal shoh ny shinney na uss,” dooyrt eh rish Wenna, as ren ee gearey.

Ghow ad y famlagh dys ny garaghyn cooidjagh ec cooyl y valley. Ta famlagh mie son y thalloo, as ta ny praaseyn gaase dy mie ayn. Va'n chairt trome, agh va Wenna as Obadiah cur lesh eh cooidjagh. Ren Wenna y ping y reayll, as t'eh eck foast.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va'n calloo goll er folmaghey?
Va ny boallaghyn echey brisht, as she egin daue ve jeant noa.
Quoi ta Obadiah Penketh?
V'eh ny varrinagh rish daeed blein, as t'eh cummal ec y phurt ayns Rhumsaa.
Cre va ec bun y calloo?
Va drundin doo ayn, as famlagh as kishtaghyn gimmee.
Cre ren Obadiah lesh y gimmagh?
Ren eh y gimmagh y chur erash 'sy cheayn.
Cre hooar Wenna 'sy drundin?
Hooar ee ping shenn veih'n vlein 1911.
Cre lesh ren Obadiah y famlagh y chiangley er y chairt?
Ren eh y famlagh y chiangley lesh yeeal shenn jeh crackan.

lessons.title: Yn skeeal aym
lessons.summary: At a community evening in Douglas, fifteen-year-old Farida Haddad tells in her own words how her family came to live on the island: in their country people of their faith suffered persecution, and her father Karim was taken prisoner and spent a year in captivity; when he was let go the family fled at night, past soldiers with weapons, to the sea, and escaped in a small boat; at the customs in England an officer was kind to them, and three years ago they came to Douglas; at first people looked at Farida's headscarf, but now the neighbours greet her, her father teaches in the library, and her little brother Sami speaks Manx at school.
lessons.text:
Ayns y thie-balley ayns Doolish, va fastyr cooidjagh son ny naboonyn. Hie Farida Haddad, inneen jeh queig bleeaney jeig, seose roish ny naboonyn, as ren ee lhaih yn skeeal eck hene:

“Ta mee baghey ayns Doolish rish three bleeaney nish. Agh cha row mee ruggit ayns shoh. Ta'n çheer aym foddey ersooyl. Ayns y çheer shen, va tranlaase er sleih yn chredjue ain. Cha dod shin goll dys y cheeill ain. Cha dod my ayr obbyr y gheddyn. Va'n tranlaase ny smessey dagh blein.

“Laa dy row, haink sidooryn gys y thie ain, as ghow ad my ayr Karim lhieu. Va ny sidooryn freayll eh myr cappee rish blein. Cha row fys ain c'raad v'eh. Tra haink eh erash, v'eh feer faase. Cha jean eh loayrt dy mennick mychione y chappeeys echey. Dooyrt eh dy row ymmodee cappeeyn elley 'sy phryssoon marish, as dy row ad mie da'n cheilley. V'eh myr cappee, agh cha row eh ny lomarcan.

“Lurg y chappeeys echey, dooyrt my ayr: ‘She egin dooin chea.’ Hea shin 'syn oie. Va sidooryn ec y raad, as wappinyn ayns nyn laueyn. Va aggle orrym roish ny wappinyn shen. Agh cha vaik ad shin. Hie shin dys y cheayn, as va baatey beg aarloo. 'Sy voghrey, va shin shaghnit. Va boggey mooar er my voir.

“Haink shin dys Sostyn. Ec y custym, va fer-oik feer ooasle. Ren eh jeeagh er ny pabyryn ain, as dooyrt eh: ‘Failt ort.’ Cha jean mee jarrood y fer shen rieau, as cha jean mee jarrood oik y custym shen. Va shin shaghnit veih'n tranlaase, agh va bea noa roin.

“Three bleeaney er dy henney, haink shin dys Mannin. Ec y toshiaght, va sleih jeeagh er my vreid. Ta mee goaill breid er my chione dagh laa, er-y-fa dy vel shen ayrn jeh'n chredjue aym. Va mee trimshagh 'sy thie, ny keayrtyn. Agh nish ta ny naboonyn gra ‘Moghrey mie, Farida!’ as cha nel monney jeeagh er y vreid. Ta my ayr ynsaghey Arabish 'sy lioarlann. Ta my vraar beg Sami loayrt Gaelg 'sy scoill, ny share na mish!

“Ta shin baghey ayns ellan veg, agh ta sleih ayn as cree mooar oc. Ta shin shaghnit, as ta shin ec y thie.”

Ren ny naboonyn ooilley bwoalley nyn laueyn.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa hea lught-thie Farida veih'n çheer oc?
Va tranlaase er sleih yn chredjue oc, as v'eh goll ny smessey.
Cre cho liauyr as va Karim myr cappee?
V'eh myr cappee rish blein.
Cre va ayns laueyn ny sidooryn ec y raad?
Va wappinyn ayns nyn laueyn.
Cre dooyrt y fer-oik ec y custym?
Dooyrt eh “Failt ort” roo.
C'raad ta'n lught-thie baghey nish?
T'ad baghey ayns Doolish rish three bleeaney.
Cre'n fa ta Farida goaill breid?
Er-y-fa dy vel y breid ayrn jeh'n chredjue eck.

lessons.title: Y pannyl ec y vargey
lessons.summary: Marmaduke Ollerenshaw was a professional baker for thirty years in a factory in Douglas that made sausages and bread; because professionals may not enter the baking competition at the village fair in Ballasalla, he sits on the panel of judges with the farmer Dorothea Fawcett: there is a big, showy cake covered in sugar flowers, thick slices of bread with aged cheese, sausage rolls, and a plain apple cake made by eleven-year-old Kit, who peeled the apples himself and used flour from the old mill; the showy cake is dry inside, and the panel chooses Kit's cake.
lessons.text:
Rish jeih bleeaney as feed, va Marmaduke Ollerenshaw gobbraghey myr fer fuinney gerrymoil ayns thie grease mooar ayns Doolish. Ayns y thie grease shen, v'ad jannoo arran as pronnagyn, as thousaneyn jeu dagh laa. Nish t'eh ny henn ghooinney, agh t'eh foast fuinney arran 'sy thie.

Dagh blein ayns Luanistyn, ta margey mooar ayns Ballasalla, as ta cloie-fuinney ayn. Cha nod sleih gerrymoil goaill ayrn 'sy chloie shen: t'ee son sleih ta fuinney 'sy thie ynrican. Myr shen, ta Marmaduke er y phannyl. Ta Dorothea Fawcett, eirinagh voish y valley, er y phannyl marish.

Va kiare red er y voayrd roish y pannyl.

Va'n chied red arran millish mooar, cho mooar as queeyl. Va ny smoo na keead blaa jeant jeh shugyr er, jiarg, buigh as gorrym. “T'eh feer haishbynagh,” dooyrt Dorothea. “Ta shen ny red taishbynagh dy jarroo,” dooyrt Marmaduke. Ren eh peesh y ghiarey. Va'n arran millish creoi as gyn blass 'sy vean.

Va peeshyn roauyr dy arran ayn neesht, as caashey eashit orroo. “Ta'n caashey shoh eashit rish daa vlein,” dooyrt Dorothea. “T'eh geyre as mie.” Agh va ny peeshyn ro roauyr. “Cha nod paitçhey y veeal y fosley cho lheead shen,” dooyrt Marmaduke, as ren ad gearey.

Eisht va pronnagyn ayns arran ayn. Ren Marmaduke pronnag y ghoaill, as ren eh smooinaghtyn er y thie grease. “Ta'n phronnag shoh ny share na pronnag erbee ren shin 'sy thie grease,” dooyrt eh.

Va'n kiarroo red beg as cadjin: arran millish ooylyn. Va ennym er pabyr beg: “Kit, 11 bleeaney.” Va Kit hene ny hassoo faggys da, as aggle er.

“Ren mee ny ooylyn y speeiney mee hene,” dooyrt eh. “Va'n speeiney liauyr, agh s'mie lhiam eh. Ta'n flooyr veih'n vwyllin shenn 'sy ghlion. Ta'n flooyr shen ny share na flooyr y shapp.”

Ren ny briwnyn blass y ghoaill. Va'n arran millish ooylyn bog as millish, as cha row eh taishbynagh er chor erbee.

Ren y pannyl loayrt cooidjagh rish tammylt. Eisht dooyrt Dorothea: “Ta'n pannyl er reih arran millish Kit.” Ren Kit lheim son boggey.

“Cha nel feme ec arran mie ve taishbynagh,” dooyrt Marmaduke rish. “Ta feme echey er ooylyn mie, flooyr mie, as traa.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad va Marmaduke gobbraghey?
V'eh gobbraghey myr fer fuinney gerrymoil ayns thie grease ayns Doolish.
Cre'n fa ta Marmaduke er y phannyl?
Er-y-fa nagh nod sleih gerrymoil goaill ayrn 'sy chloie.
Cre va er ny peeshyn roauyr dy arran?
Va caashey eashit orroo, eashit rish daa vlein.
Cre ren Kit hene?
Ren eh ny ooylyn y speeiney, as ghow eh flooyr veih'n vwyllin shenn.
Cre ren y pannyl y reih?
Ren y pannyl arran millish ooylyn Kit y reih.

lessons.title: Yn chohaglym 'sy thie-scoill shenn
lessons.summary: The old primary school in Jurby has stood empty for five years, and the education ministry will sell it; at a village meeting two factions form: the prominent businesswoman Juliana Brough and her associates want flats for young families, and the nationalist Aloysius Fenby wants a Manx language centre; the retired colonel Hereward Lascelles chairs the meeting, and he is judicious: he says the reality is that young people are leaving the village, but the language matters too, and he proposes a bargain: flats upstairs and the language centre downstairs; both factions accept it, and the ministry agrees.
lessons.text:
Ta'n vunscoill shenn ayns Jurby follym rish queig bleeaney. Ta'n airaght ynsee er ghra dy jean ee y thie y chreck. Myr shen, va cohaglym ayns y thie-scoill shenn er Jerdein, as haink ny smoo na keead dy leih.

Ec y toshiaght, va daa chologid 'sy valley.

Va Juliana Brough ec kione y chied chologid. She ben ardghooagh ee: t'ee reayll shappyn ayns ny tree baljyn, as t'ee ny h-oltey jeh coonceil y valley. Va coheshaghtagh eck marish, fer-troggee ardghooagh. “Ta feme er thieyn,” dooyrt Juliana. “Ta mee laccal thieyn beggey son lught-thie aegey 'sy scoill shenn.” Dooyrt y coheshaghtagh shen dy voddagh eh shey thieyn y hroggal ayn.

Va Aloysius Fenby ec kione y chologid elley. She ashooneyragh eh, as t'eh ynsaghey Gaelg da paitçhyn as da sleih aasit. “Ta'n scoill shoh ayrn jeh'n shennaghys ain,” dooyrt yn ashooneyragh. “Lhisagh ee ve ny thie son y Ghaelg: lioarlann veg, as shamyryn son ynsaghey.” Va e choheshaghtee bwoalley nyn laueyn.

Va'n cohaglym goll dy olk. Va'n daa chologid loayrt as streeu, as cha row unnane jeu eaishtagh rish y chologid elley.

Ec y voayrd, va shenn churnal ny hoie: Hereward Lascelles. V'eh ny churnal 'syn armee rish daeed blein, as nish t'eh cummal ayns thie beg ry-lhiattee y cheeill. Ta fys ec dy chooilley pheiagh dy vel y curnal toiggalagh. Dirree eh seose, as v'ad ooilley eaishtagh. Ta ny sleih credjal eh.

“Lhig dooin jeeagh er y feerid,” dooyrt y curnal. “Ta'n feerid shoh: ta ny sleih aegey faagail y valley, er-y-fa nagh vel thieyn oc. Agh ta feerid elley ayn neesht: ta'n Ghaelg goll er coayl, as ta feme eck er boayl. Cha nel shiu streeu noi y cheilley. Ta shiu ooilley laccal y valley y reayll bio.”

Eisht ren eh bargane y chur roue: thieyn beggey er y lhiattee heose jeh'n scoill, as thie y Ghaelg er y lhiattee heese. “Ta'n thie mooar dy liooar son y daa red,” dooyrt eh.

Ren Juliana smooinaghtyn. Ren Aloysius smooinaghtyn. Eisht ren y daa chologid soie sheese cooidjagh. “She bargane mie eh,” dooyrt Juliana. “She bargane toiggalagh eh,” dooyrt Aloysius.

Hie lettyr veih'n cohaglym dys yn airaght. Shiaghtin ny lurg shen, haink freggyrt: va'n airaght er choardail.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va cohaglym 'sy thie-scoill shenn?
Er-y-fa dy row yn airaght ynsee laccal y scoill shenn y chreck.
Quoi va ec kione ny daa chologid?
Va Juliana Brough ec kione y chied chologid, as Aloysius Fenby ec kione y chologid elley.
Quoi ta Juliana Brough?
She ben ardghooagh ee, as t'ee reayll shappyn.
Cre ta Aloysius Fenby laccal?
She ashooneyragh eh, as t'eh laccal thie son y Ghaelg.
Cre'n feerid dooyrt y curnal?
Dooyrt eh dy vel ny sleih aegey faagail y valley, as dy vel y Ghaelg goll er coayl.
Cre'n sorçh dooinney ta'n curnal?
She dooinney toiggalagh eh.
Cre va'n bargane?
Thieyn beggey heose, as thie y Ghaelg heese.

lessons.title: Oie Houney ec y shenn-voir
lessons.summary: On Hallowe'en night Hepzibah Crowther tells her grandchildren Posy and Bram the old beliefs of the island in her cottage in Sulby: people hung vervain over the door to keep the fairies out; she tells a frightening tale of a giant who threw a spear across the sea at a fairy, and of the fairy who flew away as a little feathered bird; the children carve a lantern that shines in the window, and they make a rhyme to sing at the neighbours' doors, and Hepzibah explains what the old words mean.
lessons.text:
Oie Houney v'ayn, as va'n gheay sheidey mygeayrt thie Hepzibah Crowther ayns Sulby. Va'n daa phaitçhey-vac eck, Posy as Bram, ny soie ec yn aile.

“Shenn-voir,” dooyrt Posy, “cre'n fa ta lus beg croghey er y dorrys?”

“Vervine eh,” dooyrt Hepzibah. “Va ny shenn sleih 'syn ellan shoh credjal dy row y vervine freayll ny ferrishyn ersooyl. Ta ny ferrishyn goll mygeayrt Oie Houney. Va ny sleih croghey vervine er y dorrys, as cha jinnagh ferrish erbee çheet stiagh. Ren my voir vervine y chroghey er y dorrys shoh, as ta mish jannoo eh foast.”

“Vel oo credjal ayns ferrishyn?” dooyrt Bram.

Ren Hepzibah gearey. “Cha nel mee credjal, agh cha nel mee laccal boirey y chur orroo!”

Eisht dooyrt ee: “Vel shiu laccal skeeal agglagh y chlashtyn?” Va aggle beg er ny paitçhyn, agh dooyrt ad: “Ta!”

“Er dyn, va foawragh cummal er y clieau mooar shoh. V'eh cho ard as y cheeill, as va laueyn foawragh echey. Laa dy row, ren ferrish beg gearey mysh. Ren y foawragh shleiy y ghoaill, shleiy cho liauyr as billey, as ren eh y shleiy y hilgey harrish y cheayn. Hie y shleiy derrey Nerin! Agh hie y ferrish ersooyl myr eean beg clooieagh. Va'n eean clooieagh shen etlagh harrish y cheayn, as cha dooar y foawragh rieau eh. As ta'n shleiy ayns Nerin foast, as eh ny chreg.”

“Va shen agglagh!” dooyrt Posy, as ren ee lheim.

Lurg y skeeal, ren ny paitçhyn londeyr y yannoo veih napin mooar. Ren Bram eddin agglagh y ghiarey 'sy napin, as hug Posy cainle veg stiagh. Va'n soilshey soilshean 'sy dorraghey. “Jeeagh er y soilshean echey!” dooyrt Bram. Ren ad eh y hoiaghey 'sy uinnag, son ny naboonyn.

Eisht v'ad laccal arrane y yannoo son ny dorryssyn. “She egin da arrane mie drane,” dooyrt Hepzibah. Ren ad arrane beg y yannoo: “Oie Houney, lhig dooin cloie; ta ny ferrishyn ersooyl 'syn oie!” “Ta drane eddyr ‘cloie’ as ‘oie’,” dooyrt Hepzibah. “Shen drane mie.”

“Cre ta'n fockle 'Houney' meanal?” dooyrt Bram.

“T'eh meanal toshiaght y gheurey,” dooyrt Hepzibah. “Ta'n oie shoh ec jerrey yn fouyir, roish y gheurey. As ta 'ferrish' meanal yn sleih beggey. Agh cha nel oo laccal fys y ve ayd er ooilley ny focklyn. Nish, lhig dooin goll magh as yn arrane y ghoaill!”

Feyshtyn:
Cre va croghey er y dorrys?
Va vervine croghey er y dorrys, dy reayll ny ferrishyn ersooyl.
Cre ren y foawragh y hilgey harrish y cheayn?
Ren eh shleiy liauyr y hilgey harrish y cheayn derrey Nerin.
Cre'n aght hie y ferrish ersooyl?
Hie y ferrish ersooyl myr eean beg clooieagh.
Cre va soilshean 'sy uinnag?
Va londeyr soilshean 'sy uinnag, as cainle veg ayn.
Cre ta 'Houney' meanal?
T'eh meanal toshiaght y gheurey.

lessons.title: Y sultan 'sy halley
lessons.summary: Every winter the drama club in Peel puts on a pantomime in the old church hall, in a partnership with the school; this year the director Fabienne Darrow has written a funny play about a sultan who has lost his cat; the club is not exclusive, so anyone can take part, and the shy schoolboy Emrys Pugh is chosen to play the sultan because he is a good singer, but his pitch goes wrong when he is nervous; the small orchestra of neighbours plays, the dancers come on stage in pairs, and Fabienne records a rehearsal and replays it so that Emrys can hear himself; the hall has a fine resonance, and on the night his song is perfect.
lessons.text:
Dagh geurey, ta'n sheshaght-chloie ayns Pheeil jannoo cloie son y Nollick ayns halley shenn y cheeill. Ta copharteeys eddyr y sheshaght as y scoill: ta ny paitçhyn goaill ayrn, as ta ny ynseyderyn jannoo ny eaddeeyn. Ta'n copharteeys shoh er ve ayn rish feed blein.

Ta'n sheshaght-chloie shoh fosley da dy chooilley pheiagh. “Cha nel y sheshaght ain liehlagh,” dooyrt Fabienne Darrow, y ven ta stiurey y chloie. “Ta sheshaghtyn liehlagh ayns Doolish, son sleih ta cloie myr obbyr. Ayns shoh, ta failt er dy chooilley unnane.”

Y vlein shoh, ren Fabienne cloie noa y screeu: “Y Sultan as e Chayt.” Ayns y chloie, ta sultan ayn ta cummal ayns thie-reeoil mooar. Ta'n sultan er choayl e chayt, as t'eh shirrey eh 'sy çheer ooilley.

Ren Fabienne Emrys Pugh y reih myr y sultan. Ta Emrys tree bleeaney jeig, as cha nel eh loayrt monney. Agh she arraneagh mie eh, as ta coraa aalin echey. Tra ta aggle er, cha nel y bingys echey kiart: t'eh ro ard ny ro injil.

Ta kiaullane veg ec y sheshaght. Cha nel ny kiaulleyderyn gerrymoil: she naboonyn ad, as ta'n ven-lhee cloie er y feddan. Ta'n kiaullane cloie cooidjagh dagh Jeheiney.

Ayns y chloie, ta ny daunseyryn çheet stiagh piyral, guilley as inneen, daa as daa. Ta ny daunseyryn piyral goll mygeayrt y sultan, as eisht ta'n sultan goaill e arrane.

Ec y chied aarlaghey, va aggle er Emrys, as va'n bingys echey ro injil. Ren Fabienne yn arrane echey y recortys. Eisht ren ee yn arrane y aachloie da. “Ta dty choraa mie,” dooyrt ee. “T'ou dty arraneagh dy jarroo. Eaisht rish y kiaullane, as bee'n bingys mie.” Ren ee yn arrane y aachloie three keayrtyn, as ren Emrys eaishtagh dy mie.

Er yn oie vooar, va'n halley lane. Ta aavuilley aalin ec y halley shenn: ta'n kiaull goll seose dys y thie-mullee as çheet erash, myr ayns keeill. Hie Emrys seose myr y sultan. Ren eh e arrane y ghoaill, as va'n bingys echey kiart. Va'n aavuilley cur y coraa echey dys dagh corneil jeh'n halley. Ren ny sleih ooilley bwoalley nyn laueyn.

“Va'n sultan ain yn arraneagh share 'syn ellan!” dooyrt Fabienne.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n copharteeys ta ec y sheshaght-chloie?
Ta copharteeys eddyr y sheshaght as y scoill.
Vel y sheshaght-chloie liehlagh?
Cha nel. Ta failt er dy chooilley unnane.
Cre ta'n sultan er choayl ayns y chloie?
T'eh er choayl e chayt.
Cre'n boirey va ec Emrys?
Tra va aggle er, cha row y bingys echey kiart.
Cre ren Fabienne lesh yn arrane?
Ren ee yn arrane y recortys, as eisht ren ee eh y aachloie da Emrys.
Cre'n fa va'n coraa echey aalin 'sy halley?
Er-y-fa dy vel aavuilley aalin ec y halley shenn.
Cre'n aght ta ny daunseyryn çheet stiagh?
T'ad çheet stiagh piyral, daa as daa.

lessons.title: Fastyr fo ny rollageyn
lessons.summary: Seymour Halstead worked for forty years at the stock exchange in London and now leads a small astronomy club in the village hall in Santon; twelve-year-old Elowen comes with an astrological page from a magazine and asks if the stars decide her week; Seymour explains the ecliptic, the line in the sky that the sun, the moon and the planets follow, and why astrological signs are not science; he shows his model of the sun, the earth and the moon to explain the phases of the moon and the distance to it, and outside they see a thin crescent moon; he tells them of the Phoenix, a group of stars seen only from the south; Elowen's question was a spur for everyone, and she wants to come back.
lessons.text:
Rish daeed blein, va Seymour Halstead gobbraghey 'sy voorse ayns Lunnin. Va ny ooryn liauyr 'sy voorse, as cha row traa echey jeeagh er y speyr. Nish t'eh cummal ayns Santon, as dagh mee t'eh reayll fastyr son sheshaght veg as graih oc er ny rollageyn: ny naboonyn, paitçhyn as eer y saggyrt. “Va'n boorse lane dy earrooyn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n speyr lane dy hoilshey.”

Er y Jeheiney shoh, haink Elowen, inneen jeh daa vlein jeig, as duillag veih lioar-naight ayns e laue. Va screeuyn astroaylleeagh er y duillag. “Ta'n duillag astroaylleeagh shoh gra dy bee shiaghtin vie aym, er-y-fa dy vel y ghrian ayns y rollage aym,” dooyrt ee. “Vel ny rollageyn reaghey my vea?”

She brod mie va'n feysht shen son y sheshaght ooilley.

“Feysht mie,” dooyrt Seymour. “Jeeagh. Ta raad 'sy speyr ta'n ghrian goll er, blein lurg blein. She yn ecliptagh eh. Ta'n eayst as ny plannadyn goll faggys da'n ecliptagh neesht. Ta ny rollageyn er y raad ecliptagh shen goaill ayrn ayns ny screeuyn astroaylleeagh. Agh cha nel ad reaghey dty vea. T'ad foddey, foddey ersooyl.”

Eisht hug eh lesh moddyl: bluckan buigh son y ghrian, bluckan gorrym son y theihll, as bluckan beg bane son yn eayst. Ren eh y moddyl y chasley mygeayrt. “Jeeagh er y moddyl,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n eayst goll mygeayrt y theihll dagh mee. Tra ta'n ghrian soilshaghey er y lhiattee elley jeh, cha nel shin fakin agh peesh veg jeh. Shen yn chied phaase. Eisht ta'n eayst gaase, paase lurg paase, derrey t'ee lane.”

“As yn foddid?” dooyrt Elowen. “Cre'n foddid t'ayn eddyr shin as yn eayst?”

“Ta'n foddid mysh 384000 kilometer,” dooyrt Seymour. “Ta'n moddyl shoh beg, agh ta'n foddid mooar dy jarroo.”

Hie ad ooilley magh. Va'n speyr glen, as 'syn aer, va corran thanney ny soie heose: yn eayst noa. “Ta'n corran shen yn chied phaase,” dooyrt Elowen.

“Ta sheshaght dy rollageyn ayn as cummey beaynushag urree,” dooyrt Seymour. “Ta'n veaynushag ny eean ayns shenn skeealyn: t'ee goll ayns aile, as t'ee çheet magh reesht, noa. Cha nel ny rollageyn shen ry-akin veih Mannin: she egin dhyt goll dys y yiass dy akin y veaynushag 'sy speyr.”

Lurg shen, dooyrt Elowen: “Ta mee laccal çheet erash y mee shoh çheet.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad va Seymour gobbraghey?
V'eh gobbraghey 'sy voorse ayns Lunnin rish daeed blein.
Cre va er y duillag va ec Elowen?
Va screeuyn astroaylleeagh er y duillag.
Cre va'n brod son y sheshaght?
She feysht Elowen va'n brod.
Cre ta'n ecliptagh?
She yn raad 'sy speyr ta'n ghrian goll er.
Cre va'n moddyl?
Va bluckan buigh, bluckan gorrym as bluckan beg bane ayn, son y ghrian, y theihll as yn eayst.
Cre honnick ad 'sy speyr?
Honnick ad corran thanney: yn eayst noa.
Cre ta'n veaynushag ayns shenn skeealyn?
She eean ee ta goll ayns aile, as t'ee çheet magh reesht, noa.

lessons.title: Y pirgrin dys y cheeill er y chronk
lessons.summary: Every June the people of the parish walk a pilgrimage from Ramsey to an old ruined chapel on a hill, which stands in a small enclosure inside a stone wall; seventy-two-year-old Mildred Jessop walks it for the first time with her new hip, in a waterproof coat, and her neighbour Hubert Lomax, a nurse, carries a first-aid box; a young pilgrim gets a painful lump on his foot and a scratch from brambles, and Hubert cleans the wound because of bacterial illness and explains the secretion from the skin; at the chapel the pilgrims pray, sing and eat together inside the enclosure, and Mildred is proud of her hip.
lessons.text:
Dagh blein ayns Mean Souree, ta sleih y skeerey goll er pirgrin. T'ad shooyl veih Rhumsaa dys keeill shenn er y chronk, kiare meeiley ersooyl. Cha nel agh ny boallaghyn faagit jeh'n cheeill, agh ta'n raad ny raad pirgrin rish ymmodee cheead blein. Ta ny pirgrinyn shooyl cooidjagh, loayrt as goaill arraneyn.

Y vlein shoh, va Mildred Jessop goll er y pirgrin son y chied cheayrt. Ta Mildred daa vlein as three-feed. Ayns Averil, hooar ee lhesh noa 'sy thie-lhee. Va pian ayns y shenn lhesh eck rish bleeantyn. “Ta'n lhesh noa shoh ny share na'n lhesh va aym tra va mee aeg!” dooyrt ee.

Va cooat jeenagh urree, as v'ee jeenagh noi'n fliaghey. Va'n naboo eck, Hubert Lomax, shooyl marish. She boandyr eh, as v'eh cur lesh kishtey couyr: lheeys, eaddagh glen as ushtey. “Ta couyr lhee aym son dy chooilley pheiagh,” dooyrt eh.

Ec y vean-laa, va guilley aeg shooyl dy moal. Va moyl jiarg er e chass, faggys da'n vraag. “Ta'n vraag ro veg,” dooyrt eh. Ren Hubert jeeagh er y voyl. “T'ou er ve shooyl rish ooryn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n moyl shoh çheet veih'n vraag.” Hug eh eaddagh bog er y voyl.

Va lhott beg er laue y ghuilley neesht, veih tom ec y raad. Ren Hubert y lhott y ghlenney dy mie lesh ushtey glen. “Cha nel y lhott mooar,” dooyrt eh, “agh foddee gorley bacteyragh çheet stiagh ayn. Ta gorley bacteyragh ny smessey na lhott.” Va taaley beg buigh çheet ass y lhott. “Ta'n taaley shoh cadjin,” dooyrt Hubert. “Ta'n crackan jannoo taaley tra t'eh gortit. Ta'n taaley shoh glenney yn lhott.”

“Cre'n aght t'ou shooyl cho mie?” dooyrt y guilley rish Mildred. Ren ee gearey. “Ta'n lhesh noa aym, as ta cooat jeenagh orrym!”

Ec y jerrey, haink ad dys y cheeill. Ta'n cheeill ny soie ayns paal beg, as boalley clagh mygeayrt y phaal. Hie ny pirgrinyn ooilley stiagh 'sy phaal. Ren y saggyrt padjer, as ren ad arrane y ghoaill. Eisht ren ad soie er y faiyr 'sy phaal, as ren ad arran as tey y ghoaill cooidjagh.

“Va mee jeenagh noi'n fliaghey, as va'n lhesh aym lajer,” dooyrt Mildred. “Bee mee er y pirgrin reesht y vlein shoh çheet.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta sleih y skeerey jannoo ayns Mean Souree?
T'ad goll er pirgrin dys keeill shenn er y chronk.
Cre hooar Mildred ayns Averil?
Hooar ee lhesh noa 'sy thie-lhee.
Cre va Hubert cur lesh?
V'eh cur lesh kishtey couyr, as lheeys, eaddagh glen as ushtey ayn.
Cre va er cass y ghuilley?
Va moyl jiarg er e chass, veih'n vraag.
Cre'n fa ren Hubert y lhott y ghlenney?
Er-y-fa dy vod gorley bacteyragh çheet stiagh ayn.
C'raad ta'n cheeill ny soie?
T'ee ny soie ayns paal beg, as boalley clagh mygeayrt.
